statements.t: In the fourth quarter of 2026, we currently expect NBSK pulp prices to increase modestly across our markets due to continued global supply constraints.
We currently expect lumber prices to be relatively flat in the fourth quarter of 2026, as weak demand, driven by high interest rates and seasonal slowdowns, is offset by ongoing supply constraints.
We anticipate pallet prices to remain flat in the fourth quarter due to continued weak economic conditions in Europe and mass timber prices to remain relatively steady.

For the fourth quarter of 2026, per unit fiber costs for our German pulp mills are expected to increase slightly, driven by continued strong demand for wood as an energy source amid ongoing geopolitical conflicts, and reduced supply.

Conversely, per unit fiber costs for our Canadian pulp mills are expected to decrease following renegotiation of Celgar’s supply contracts and improved supply, while sawmill per unit fiber costs are projected to remain flat.

The Company expects to complete the Restructuring by the end of calendar year 2026.

In the nine months ended September 30, 2025, we received $5.0 million in government grants for capital projects at our Celgar mill and mass timber facilities.

Our demand loan facility and Canadian standby letter of credit facility are expected to remain unchanged and outstanding or to receive such other treatment as is reasonably agreed to by the Company Parties, the required Consenting Senior Noteholders and the holder of the applicable facility.
